name: Vepugratinib
summary: Vepugratinib (LY3866288, LOXO-435) is Lilly's oral, isoform-selective FGFR3 inhibitor. The pivotal trial is FORAGER-2 (NCT07218380). It is a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 adding vepugratinib to enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EV+P) in untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with an FGFR3 alteration. The primary endpoint is PFS by blinded central review, and primary completion is 2029-10. Price anchor: Balversa (erdafitinib), the only marketed FGFR inhibitor in urothelial cancer, at $74,345 per CMS Part D beneficiary in 2024. Uptake anchor: EV+P, the regimen vepugratinib is added to, reached 51% of US first-line la/mUC patients in 2024, its first full year (Flatiron, ASCO GU 2026).

therapy_mode.source: FORAGER-2 design (NCT07218380; ASCO GU 2026 TPS895, doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.7_suppl.TPS895): oral daily vepugratinib added to EV+P, with PFS as the primary endpoint
therapy_mode.note: Oncology treated to progression, so chronic by the house definition

list_price_per_patient.source: lookup.py demand Balversa: CMS Medicare Part D 2024, $22,675,187.94 over 305 beneficiaries = $74,345 per beneficiary
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement: house convention. Balversa is the closest marketed comparator: the only approved FGFR inhibitor in urothelial cancer, and oral like vepugratinib. The case against is that it is used later-line as monotherapy, with a median PFS of 5.6 months in THOR (NEJM 2023, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2308849). A beneficiary's spend therefore covers well under a year of therapy, and this figure understates an annual price. Retail quotes of about $28,000 a month for 8 mg daily (drugs.com, GoodRx) would annualise to roughly $330,000, but that is not a named manufacturer list price, so the convention stands. A reviewer may also argue that a first-line add-on to an IV regimen would be priced below monotherapy. The two effects pull in opposite directions.

gross_to_net_pct.source: house convention on a CMS per-beneficiary price (halving lands at a median 96% of CMS negotiated net prices)
gross_to_net_pct.note: Direction checked: 0.5 off list, so net is $37,172 per patient-year

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39, 2.5-year follow-up (Annals of Oncology 2025, PMID 40460988): median PFS 12.5 months (95% CI 10.4-16.6) on EV+P, the backbone and control arm of FORAGER-2
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/12.5) = 0.486, the form the ABBV-1480 seed uses. The brief's 1 - exp(-12/12.5) gives 0.617. That formula treats the median as a mean, so I did not use it. The case against: FORAGER-2 is designed to extend PFS beyond EV+P, and median duration of treatment on an add-on can be shorter than PFS because of toxicity-driven stops. The FGFR3-altered subgroup of EV-302 may also differ from the all-comer median.

forecast_start_year.note: Launch is clearly later than 2027: readout around late 2029, filing in 2030, and US launch expected around late 2030 on a standard review. 2031 is the first full year on market. Judgement on the review timeline

exus_multiple.source: Verzenio FY2025: $2,259mm outside the US against $3,464mm US (LLY 10-K 0000059478-26-000013; Q4 2025 release, 0000059478-26-000008)
exus_multiple.note: Judgement on the comparator. Verzenio is Lilly's own mature oral targeted oncology drug and has a clean filed geographic split. Padcev cannot serve: Pfizer books only $38mm outside the US because Astellas sells it there. Balversa's split is not disclosed by J&J. The case against: Verzenio is a breast-cancer drug with long treatment duration, and ex-US access for a first-line FGFR3 add-on to an expensive EV+P regimen may be thinner

economics_share.source: Lilly oncology pipeline (lillyoncologypipeline.com/molecule/fgfr3-inhibitor/clinical-trial/NCT07218380); Lilly is lead sponsor of NCT07218380, NCT07827612 and NCT05614739
economics_share.note: Loxo@Lilly internal molecule (LOXO-435). No partner found in filings or search

prevalence.note: Carried by the book. See untreated_carryover_pct: the book's prevalence is the whole living bladder-cancer population, and this is a line of therapy

eligible_pct.source: Two filters. (1) 11,600 US patients a year receive first-line therapy for la/mUC, out of about 22,542 diagnosed with or progressing to la/mUC (systematic review and flow model, J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2021, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2020.20285). (2) FGFR3 known or likely pathogenic alteration in 281 of 1,416 mUC patients, 20% (Clinical and Genomic Landscape of FGFR3 Alterations Across Different Stages of Urothelial Cancer, Eur Urol Open Sci 2025, PMID 40521274). 11,600 x 0.20 = 2,320 a year, over the book's 84,530 incidence = 0.0274
eligible_pct.note: Stated as a share of incidence. The 11,600 dates from a flow model built on an incidence near 81,000, so it is a slightly older base. The case for a lower figure: a nationwide registry finds FGFR3 in about 15% of metastatic cases. The label pool includes upper-tract disease, which FORAGER-2 enrols and which the SEER bladder count excludes. Applied to the book's 763,031 prevalence this gives an opening stock of 20,942, which a first-line pool does not have. See untreated_carryover_pct

untreated_carryover_pct.source: forecast.py convention for a line of cancer therapy (a patient not started this year starts another drug and leaves the line)
untreated_carryover_pct.note: Added because the book's pool for this disease has prevalence far above incidence. Without it the engine would draw down a prevalent stock of 20,942 first-line patients that does not exist. Even at 0.0 the engine still counts that opening stock in year one, which overstates year one about 10x at a small ramp value. The cleaner fix is an asset-level prevalence equal to incidence, but the brief forbids a second figure for one disease, so this is left for the engine owner

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of each year's eligible patients
penetration_peak_pct.source: EV+P took 420 of 821 US first-line la/mUC patients (51%) in 2024, from 15% in 2023 and 0.4% in 2022 (Flatiron Health Research Database, ASCO GU 2026, reported by UroToday: 'Real-world Use and Effectiveness of First-line Enfortumab Vedotin with Pembrolizumab in Patients with Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma in the US')
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0. Vepugratinib is an add-on to EV+P, so its ceiling is the share of FGFR3-altered first-line patients who receive EV+P. The peak is set at EV+P's measured capture. The case for lower: incomplete FGFR3 testing before first-line therapy, added FGFR toxicity (hyperphosphataemia, ocular and nail events) on top of EV's neuropathy and rash, and the fact that a positive PFS result is not guaranteed to change practice. The case for higher: EV+P share was still rising after 2024

ramp_steepness.source: book: Enhertu's CMS Part B launch fit (864, 1,904, 4,841, 7,105, 8,410 beneficiaries 2020-2024), k=1.08, midpoint 2.2 years, as carried by the ABBV-1480 and camizestrant seeds
ramp_steepness.note: Reused measured oncology curve. The book has no pipeline urothelial seed to reuse. EV+P's own first-line uptake (0.4% to 15% to 51% over 2022-2024) was steeper, but it rode an accelerated approval and replaced chemotherapy. An add-on needing a biomarker test is likely slower

ramp_midpoint_year.source: as ramp_steepness (Enhertu fit carried in the book)
